_comment: Months and weekdays drawn as a calendar page, not searched for and not clozed (tunatale-xykz, the user 2026-09-28). Each word in `words` maps to a language-neutral concept in app.cards.calendar_scenes.CALENDAR_CONCEPTS: `month_1`..`month_12` then `weekday_1`..`weekday_7` in ISO order, where 1 is Monday and 7 is Sunday. A photo search CANNOT serve this vocabulary at all: asked for 'Mars' it returns a march of people, asked for 'mandag' a photographer's choice of weekday. What these words name is a POSITION in a structure, so the picture is the structure — a year as a 4x3 grid, a week as a row of seven — with the one cell the word points at lit. `week_start` is DATA, in this file, because which day opens a week is a local custom rather than a fact about calendars; Norwegian and Slovene open on Monday, the two Philippine decks on Sunday, which is their common printed layout. It is read from here by app.cards.calendar_picture.load_calendar and handed to the renderer as an argument, so the renderer's own copy of the order cannot make the test pass. It is also in every picture's FILENAME, because the two orders draw different pages for the same concept and a shared name would serve one language's Monday card the other's page. A word in `words` is NOT a function word, whatever `function_words.json` or a POS tag says, so a month never goes down the cloze route its UPOS would otherwise pick. The veto is asked about a bare token and cannot see a SENSE, so the picture is drawn only when the card's English gloss names the month or the day (app.cards.calendar_picture.gloss_matches) — which is what keeps `mars`, both the third month and the planet, on the right route for each. Only the primary spellings are listed: there is no second form to accommodate here, so every word maps to exactly one concept.
